Supaprod is a closed-source commercial product, so the licence requirement alone is disqualifying as the programme was last written - a fit problem to solve by changing the product, not the pitch. $100k fully non-dilutive is attractive enough to justify a periodic check for a new cycle and a new theme, but this should not consume application time now. Two years of page staleness also suggests the programme may not be running.

programmes.hard_blocker: DOMAIN MISMATCH. Nucleate is a biotech and life-sciences organisation - "the largest global community of bio-innovators" whose Activator is "designed for academic biotech founders" refining "scientific discoveries into biotech venture theses", accelerating "academic bioventures" that solve "pressing biomedical and ecological challenges". Supaprod is a software product-lifecycle system and falls entirely outside the stated scope.
programmes.notes: LISTED ONLY BECAUSE THE LANE BRIEF NAMED "NUCLEATE-STYLE PROGRAMMES", AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE STYLE IS WORTH COPYING BUT THE INSTANCE IS NOT APPLICABLE. The model - a free, non-dilutive, student-led, domain-specific fellowship with heavyweight advisors and a pitch showcase - is genuinely attractive. NO SOFTWARE OR AI-TOOLING EQUIVALENT OF NUCLEATE SURFACED IN THIS SWEEP. The closest analogues found are Sundai Club (community, no funding, Boston, login-gated) and the university accelerators (MIT delta v, The House Fund, StartX), all of which gate on institutional affiliation. That gap is itself a finding: there is no affiliation-free, non-dilutive, domain-specific fellowship for applied AI software founders in the US market as it currently stands.
